newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Burundi leader in talks on economic sanctions.
newsitem.headline: Burundi leader in talks on economic sanctions.

text.p: The international mediator for the conflict in Burundi, Julius Nyerere, held talks with the Burundi military leader, Major Pierre Buyoya, in western Tanzania, on Saturday, Tanzanian radio reported.
It was the fifth round of talks between the two since Buyoya seized power in July.

The radio said the three-hour meeting at the town of Butiama focused on the economic sanctions imposed on Burundi by regional leaders after the military takeover which brought Buyoya to power. It gave no further details.

Diplomats said Buyoya's repeated calls for the lifting of the economic sanctions had been strengthened by the change in the situation in eastern Zaire, with hundreds of thousands of Rwandan refugees returning to their homeland in the last few days.
The neighbouring African states who imposed the sanctions have called for the restoration of democratic rule in Burundi.
The Burundi government said last week that Nyerere, a former Tanzanian president, had postponed what would have been the first all-party peace talks since the July coup in Burundi.
The talks would have been the first official meeting between the Burundian government and Hutu rebels.

Buyoya was invited to the talks in Arusha, north Tanzania, along with Hutu rebel leader Leonard Nyangoma of the National Council for the Defence of Democracy (CNDD) and the main political parties Frodebu and Uprona.
East African states who imposed sanctions on Burundi are demanding unconditional all-party talks as the last remaining pre-condition for the lifting of the blockade.
Two other conditions set by the regional states in September -- allowing political parties and restoring the National Assembly suspended during the coup -- have been met.
But the Burundi regime has said it will negotiate only after sanctions are relaxed.
Burundi's civil war, which has left 150,000 dead in three years, has slipped down the regional agenda because of the new crisis in eastern Zaire.
